newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Duisenberg sees most EU states in EMU by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg sees most EU states in EMU by 2000.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg said on Friday he expected a "great majority" of the 15 European Union states to be participating in economic and monetary union (EMU) by the year 2000.
Duisenberg, addressing a business conference, said five unspecified EU states already met the criteria for EMU entry and that the others were "on their way" to meet them.
"I think that by the year 2000 there will be a great majority of European Union member states participating in monetary union," he said.
Duisenberg told his audience they should not be impressed by one-off measures which countries might take to fulfil the EMU entry criteria: "It's the sustainability which is important."

The Dutch central bank president is due to take over on July 1 as head of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), the forerunner of the European Central Bank (ECB), which is scheduled to run monetary policy under EMU from 1999.
He is also widely regarded as a strong candidate to become the first president of the ECB.
